profile.campus: AWS Ohio (US-EAST-2) -- New Albany campus, Franklin / Licking / Union counties
profile.address: 14114, Jug Street Road Northwest, New Albany International Business Park, New Albany, Jersey Township, Licking County, Ohio, 43054
profile.reading:
This building is one of the data center structures Amazon Web Services operates around New Albany, Ohio, a Columbus suburb spanning Franklin, Licking, and Union counties, the physical location of AWS's US-EAST-2 cloud region.

AWS's Ohio buildout has been documented in stages by the company, the City of New Albany, and Ohio trade and local press. The City of New Albany reported in August 2025 that AWS's cumulative capital investment in the area had reached $6.2 billion since 2015, that AWS had invested $19.7 billion across Ohio over that period, and that AWS operations in New Albany had contributed $1.4 billion to Licking County gross domestic product; the city's release also cited a further $10 billion in Ohio expansion AWS announced in 2024 and a forecast $23 billion cumulative investment by 2030. In August 2023, New Albany City Council approved a further $3.5 billion AWS investment covering five additional data center buildings, according to 10TV and Data Center Frontier coverage of that council vote. CoStar separately reported in 2024 that AWS's disclosed Ohio data center investment had grown by a further $10 billion. The City of New Albany's 2025 release stated AWS had completed and staffed two data center buildings in the area, with additional facilities under construction and expected to become operational later that year, and that AWS-related activity supported an estimated 1,550 full time equivalent jobs annually in Licking County and paid $3.1 million in property taxes and fees to the county in 2024.

AWS has not published a street address, opening date, floor area, or IT power rating for this individual building, and none of the city, county, or trade press coverage found for this page breaks the New Albany campus down building by building. This structure is treated as part of the documented AWS Ohio footprint described above.

City of New Albany materials disclose cumulative investment, jobs, and GDP figures for the AWS campus as a whole, and report that two buildings were complete and staffed as of August 2025, but do not assign capacity, square footage, or opening dates to individual structures.

profile.regional_context: New Albany, a Columbus, Ohio suburb, has become one of the Midwest's fastest growing data center markets since AWS selected the area for its Ohio cloud region in the mid-2010s. American Electric Power's Ohio utility serves the corridor and has filed with state regulators over large-load data center interconnection requests as the New Albany, Licking County, and Union County buildout has expanded. Ohio offers a data center sales and use tax exemption administered by the state Development Services Agency, tied to minimum investment and payroll commitments, which local officials and trade press credit with drawing AWS and other operators to the corridor. New Albany markets itself alongside Intel's nearby semiconductor investment in Licking County as part of a broader technology corridor sometimes called the Silicon Heartland, and hosts data center campuses for other operators including Meta and Google in addition to AWS. Local governments in New Albany, Licking County, and Union County have negotiated a series of tax abatement and community benefit agreements with AWS, documented in city council minutes and covered by 10TV and Data Center Frontier.

reading.body:
AWS operates this building as part of its us-east-2 cloud region serving the Midwest. The specific building's power capacity is not published by AWS, which does not disclose per-facility technical specifications as a stated security policy. One industry index estimates the broader New Albany campus at roughly 500 MW operational capacity, though AWS itself has not confirmed this figure or broken it down to individual buildings.

The New Albany campus, spanning parts of Licking, Franklin, and Union counties, represents a documented multi-billion dollar investment by AWS announced in phases since at least 2023. The City of New Albany credits this footprint with contributing $1.4 billion to Licking County GDP and approved a 30-year local tax abatement to support continued buildout. Within Ohio, which hosts eight data center facilities with published megawatt figures totaling 60.4 MW, the New Albany campus as a whole ranks ninth by disclosed capacity, though most mapped facilities in the state publish no specification at all.

This individual building cannot be assessed for its role in AI scaling without AWS publishing per-facility power specifications. The campus matters to AI compute availability in the region insofar as it hosts the us-east-2 infrastructure, and the scale of public investment commitments suggests material capacity, but the operator's nondisclosure policy means no independent verification of this specific building's contribution to grid-constrained AI scaling is possible.
